fault_line: Intercepted or hit? The coalition says all five missiles were shot down -- witnesses say the Aramco tower was damaged anyway. Was it a leak through the shield, falling debris, or a Saturday strike surfacing a day late?

sections.what_happened: [ATTRIBUTED REPORT -- AFP witnesses] Multiple witnesses told AFP on Sunday that Riyadh's financial district was targeted and the area's Aramco building was damaged, after the Saudi-led coalition said it had intercepted missiles launched by Yemen's Ansar Allah toward the capital. One witness, referring to the King Abdullah Financial District (KAFD): 'Aramco tower in KAFD has been targeted, that's the sure thing.' Two other witnesses confirmed seeing damage to the building. [ATTRIBUTED REPORT -- Reuters] A tower in KAFD was damaged by a projectile on Sunday, said one witness and three people briefed on the matter. [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM -- coalition, unchanged from 1100-01] The coalition says air defences intercepted and destroyed five missiles on Sunday morning: 2 ballistic toward Riyadh, 1 ballistic toward the Eastern Province, 2 cruise in Riyadh and the southern regions; at least 15 missiles/UAVs intercepted across the Kingdom in November. [NO OFFICIAL COMMENT] Saudi authorities did not immediately respond to requests for comment; Aramco has not commented; no casualty report. [CONTEXT] Ansar Allah has NOT claimed a Sunday launch. Spokesman Yahya Saree's Saturday six-operations claim (recorded Nov 7 at 2100-01) included Aramco oil storage/distillation targets in Riyadh, Khurais and Pumping Station No. 8 Dawadmi; Saudi Arabia has NOT confirmed damage from those claimed strikes. Whether Sunday's damaged tower was hit by a missile that got through, by intercept debris, or during Saturday's claimed operations is NOT established by any source.
sections.what_verified: 2 distinct tiered publisher families on the damage claim: AFP (T1) and Reuters (T1). FirstPost, Turkiye Today, Hurriyet Daily News, Times of Israel (T3), Al Bawaba, NewsBytes, NN24 and jbiznews all carry the AFP wire (same family, not independent). Devdiscourse carries the Reuters wire (same family).
sections.what_disputed: The coalition says all five Sunday missiles were intercepted and destroyed; Saudi Civil Defence said the danger had passed. No Saudi or Aramco statement confirms damage, and no images of the damage have been published in-window. Ansar Allah has not claimed a Sunday launch, so no claimant ties the damage to a specific Sunday missile; the Saturday six-operations claim is the only Ansar Allah statement naming Aramco targets in Riyadh, and it remains unverified. The 1100-01 record stated 'no casualties or damage reported from Sunday's intercepts' -- that line is now superseded by the witness reports, not by an official correction.
sections.why_matters: They said all five were shot down. Witnesses say the Aramco tower was hit anyway. The first reported damage to a Riyadh financial-district tower in this round -- and neither Riyadh nor Aramco will confirm or deny it. Hard number in the title: 5 intercepted, 1 tower hit.

totw_analysis: Our read: They said all five were shot down. Witnesses say the Aramco tower was hit anyway. The first reported damage to a Riyadh financial-district tower in this round -- and neither Riyadh nor Aramco will confirm or deny it. Hard number in the title: 5 intercepted, 1 tower hit. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Intercepted or hit? The coalition says all five missiles were shot down -- witnesses say the Aramco tower was damaged anyway.
